key_insight: The paper learns phase-field equations from molecular dynamics, combining ab initio accuracy with mesoscopic-scale simulation of microstructure evolution.
engineering_relevance: This enables predictive materials design for processes like phase separation and nucleation at scales that are too large for atomistic simulation but too detailed for classical phenomenological models.
method: Derive a mesoscopic phase-field equation via Mori-Zwanzig projection of MD onto species-density fields.
Represent the unknown nonlocal free energy and mobility with neural networks.
Train on short MD trajectories generated by machine-learning interatomic potentials with ab initio accuracy.
evidence_signal: Validated on iron-boron melts and hydrogen-helium mixtures, including FeB4 pressure-dependent stability and helium-rain dynamics in a system corresponding to 2.2 million atoms.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the underlying MD trajectories and the assumptions used in the projection/closure, so transferability outside trained compositions and conditions may be limited.
